stories.headline: DR Congo Files ICJ Case Against Rwanda Over Decades of Cross-Border Conflict
stories.summary:
The Democratic Republic of Congo filed a case against Rwanda at the International Court of Justice on Friday, accusing its neighbor of violating multiple international treaties by dispatching forces and backing armed groups to carry out unlawful military operations on Congolese territory. Congolese Justice Minister Guillaume Andali said his country is seeking accountability for alleged breaches of conventions covering genocide prevention, racial discrimination, women's rights, and torture.

Rwanda has not yet responded to the filing but has long dismissed evidence that it supports the M23 rebel group, which captured large parts of the mineral-rich eastern DRC, including the regional capital Goma, in January. UN experts and Western governments have stated that Rwanda backs M23. The fighting has continued despite a U.S.-brokered peace deal signed in December.

The roots of the conflict trace back to the 1994 Rwandan genocide, after which an estimated one million Hutus fled into what is now DR Congo, stoking ethnic tensions that have fueled successive armed conflicts and foreign interventions for over three decades. This is DR Congo's third attempt to bring Rwanda before the ICJ; previous cases were dropped or dismissed on jurisdictional grounds. The ICJ will now examine the claims and consider Congo's request that Rwanda cease alleged crimes and pay reparations.

stories.headline: Update: Republican Ohio Governor Calls Supreme Court TPS Ruling 'A Mistake' as State Faces Haitian Migrant Uncertainty
stories.summary:
Ohio Governor Mike DeWine, a Republican, publicly criticized the Supreme Court's Thursday ruling in Mullin v. Doe, which cleared the way for the Trump administration to end Temporary Protected Status for Haitians and Syrians residing in the United States. DeWine, whose state is home to more than 10,000 Haitian migrants — many in the Dayton and Columbus areas — called the decision a policy mistake, even while acknowledging it as a legal ruling.

The governor's dissent from his own party's position illustrates the practical tensions the ruling creates for Republican-led states that have absorbed large immigrant communities over recent years. DeWine has previously argued that Haitian immigrants have contributed economically and culturally to Ohio communities that were facing population decline.

The ruling represents one of the Trump administration's most significant immigration victories, with the Supreme Court also separately allowing border turnback policies. Supporters of the TPS terminations argue the protections were meant to be temporary and that their extension has become indefinite, incentivizing illegal immigration. Critics, including immigrant advocacy groups and some local officials, warn the decision could separate families and destabilize communities that have come to depend on these workers.

stories.headline: Trump-Meloni Alliance Fractures Further After Trump Claims Italian PM 'Begged' for Photo
stories.summary:
The once-celebrated political alliance between U.S. President Donald Trump and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has deteriorated sharply following a series of public confrontations over the past several months. What began as one of the most closely watched partnerships in Western politics — Meloni held a front-row seat at Trump's January 2025 inauguration and later served as a key EU interlocutor during tariff negotiations — has fractured over Italy's refusal to allow U.S. military aircraft to use a NATO airbase in Sicily and Meloni's public rebuke of Trump's attack on Pope Leo XIV.

The latest rupture came after the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains in France, where officials from both sides described a productive meeting and reduced tensions. Within days, Trump told an Italian broadcaster that Meloni had "begged" him for a photograph at the summit, saying he "felt sorry for her" — comments that were aired in Italy but never released in English. Meloni responded publicly and sharply.

The falling-out carries significant diplomatic weight. Meloni had positioned her closeness to Trump as evidence of her credibility on the international stage and as leverage in managing EU-U.S. relations on tariffs and other issues. Analysts note that Trump's unpredictability has repeatedly undermined European leaders who sought to cultivate personal ties with him. Italy is a NATO member and a major economy, and the relationship's deterioration complicates transatlantic coordination at a sensitive moment.

stories.headline: Update: Venezuela Earthquake Death Toll Reaches 920 as Families Search Rubble Without Government Aid
stories.summary:
The death toll from Venezuela's back-to-back 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes has climbed to at least 920, with more than 51,000 people reported missing nearly two days after the disaster struck. Citizens in the hardest-hit areas, particularly La Guaira just north of Caracas, have taken search and rescue operations into their own hands, reporting a near-absence of government rescue teams despite official statements projecting a robust state response.

Families used hammers and power tools to cut through collapsed concrete slabs in search of buried relatives, as aid agencies warned that the critical 48-to-72-hour window for finding survivors alive was closing. Venezuelan authorities announced Friday night they would block access to La Guaira without official permits, citing chaos and traffic hampering search efforts — a move that drew alarm from residents already frustrated by inadequate help.

Acting President Delcy Rodríguez, who assumed leadership after the disaster, said the government was mounting a full response and welcomed international aid. Dozens of rescue teams from around the world have arrived or are en route. The disaster presents an enormous governance challenge for Venezuela, which was already facing a severe humanitarian and political crisis before the quakes struck.

stories.headline: U.S. Government Lifts Export Restrictions on Anthropic's Most Advanced AI Model
stories.summary:
The U.S. government has lifted its export ban on Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5, its most powerful artificial intelligence model, allowing the company to share it with more than 100 select companies and partners. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick confirmed the decision in a letter to Anthropic, with the company stating the restrictions had been resolved after the Trump administration reviewed concerns about the technology's potential national security implications.

Separately, OpenAI announced Friday it will preview its newest GPT-5.6 model series — including variants named Sol, Terra, and Luna — with a select group of partners before a broader public rollout, also at the behest of the U.S. government. The coordinated approach signals a new framework in which Washington is actively managing the release cadence of frontier AI systems before they reach the wider market.

The moves represent a significant shift in federal AI policy, with the government playing a gatekeeper role for the most capable commercial AI models. The decisions follow months of tension between AI developers and regulators over dual-use risks, and come as the U.S. seeks to maintain competitive dominance over China in advanced AI development.

stories.headline: Trump Religious Liberty Commission Report Calls for 'Building Bridges' Between Church and State
stories.summary:
A draft final report from President Trump's Religious Liberty Commission, released Friday, calls for "building bridges between church and state" — language that represents a direct departure from the longstanding American legal doctrine of church-state separation rooted in the First Amendment's Establishment Clause. The report states that "Americans must know their rights and stand with courage when those rights are challenged."

The commission's framing signals a continued push by the Trump administration to expand the role of religion in public life and government, building on prior executive actions including support for faith-based organizations receiving federal funding and the promotion of religious exemptions from federal regulations. Supporters argue the shift corrects what they see as decades of government hostility toward religious expression in the public square.

Critics, including civil liberties groups and many constitutional scholars, contend that replacing separation with a "bridges" framework risks eroding protections against government establishment of religion and could disadvantage non-Christian or non-religious Americans. The report's recommendations are expected to inform future executive actions and potential legislative proposals on religious liberty.

stories.headline: Newsom Calls for National 'Billionaires' Tax' While Opposing Similar Measure in California
stories.summary:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom, widely seen as a prospective 2028 presidential candidate, published a sweeping economic agenda Friday calling for a national minimum tax on individuals with a net worth above $100 million, new restrictions on borrowing against stock portfolios to avoid taxes, revised inheritance tax rules, and a restoration of corporate tax rates to pre-Trump levels. He also proposed a national public equity fund that would give every American a stake in artificial intelligence companies, arguing that AI-driven wealth concentration threatens democracy.

The announcement came one day after a major California health care union pledged to advance a state ballot measure imposing a one-time 5% tax on the assets of California-based billionaires — a measure Newsom opposes. He argues that taxing wealth at the state level is ineffective because billionaires can relocate to lower-tax states, and that the problem requires a federal solution. California, home to more billionaires than any other state, has seen repeated debates over whether high taxes drive out wealthy residents.

Newsom's proposals align him with the Democratic Party's populist left and mark a clear positioning ahead of a potential presidential run. Conservatives have pointed to the contradiction of Newsom championing higher taxes nationally while blocking them in his own state, arguing it reflects political opportunism rather than coherent policy. Supporters counter that his logic — that only federal action can prevent billionaires from tax-shopping between states — is economically sound.
